## Historical audit: S0084

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are to this file. Only chunk 3 is visible; the reference and rendered images are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, JSONL line 18, characters [0,299136) | The stated goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate editable geometry, matching viewpoint, framing and materials. The student interpreted it as a woodworking room; that semantic interpretation is not independently verified here. |
| Same event, first build and step 1 result | Code specified architecture, shelves, a bench, numerous tools, a bottle and trays; grouped components, rotations, camera, lights, wood-grain and metallic materials. Step 1 timed out after 600 seconds with no usable render. The cause was not established by a traceback. |
| Same event, replacement and step 2 result | The student autonomously treated complexity/render cost as a timeout hypothesis, replaced filleted shapes with boxes, reduced detail and requested Eevee while retaining the camera. Step 2 reported `ok: true` and a usable saved render. The runner log shows 16 samples, so the effective renderer should not be inferred solely from the program’s Eevee setting. |
| Same event, review and step 3 result | The student reported that step 2 was too pale, the wall ended inside the frame, and hanging squares had sideways silhouettes. It darkened materials and lighting, raised walls, rotated squares, expanded foreground geometry and retained the camera. Step 3 also reported a usable render. These are the student’s visual diagnoses, not independent confirmation of improvement. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 19, [0,3948); `model_response`, line 20, [0,373); `select`, line 21, [0,59) | The final read-only session had the reference and two render images supplied, no tool events, and returned `SELECT 3`; the select event records step 3. This establishes selection, not visual or geometric correctness. |

**Scene checks.** Multiple objects and constituent parts are explicitly constructed in code, with wood and metal shaders, procedural texture, and object rotations. Grouping does not establish physical contact or correct part connections; neither pose nor occlusion is independently verified. Camera and lighting parameters were specified; the student identified wall/framing and brightness issues but did not change the camera. The initial timeout is a technical interruption, followed by two formally usable renders—not proof of reconstruction success.

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, or receipt of teacher guidance is visible in this chunk. The runner’s failure and comparison prompts are operational feedback, distinct from teacher input. The student’s own repair and revision are visible; no additional tool-based exploration is logged in the final session.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferable: separate a no-output timeout from visual failure, simplify a build, and validate a subsequent render. Task-specific: the chosen wall height, darker palette and square rotations respond to this student’s reported comparison. Whether complexity caused the timeout, whether step 3 actually improved the match, and whether materials, object connections, camera and lighting match the photograph remain unresolved. Earlier chunks and unseen images cannot settle those questions here.
